highlights.title: Trump unveils 'Super Intelligence Force' to oversee AI policy
highlights.summary: The president named his national intelligence chief as the taskforce's head as worries over AI grow.
body: US President Donald Trump says he has created a new task force focused on artificial intelligence, which will be led by Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton.

The "Super Intelligence Force" will work to ensure that the US continues to lead in the technology's development and will coordinate the government's engagement with the public, Trump posted on Sunday.
Federal Trade Commission Chair Andrew Ferguson and Undersecretary of Defense for Research and Engineering Emil Michael will also be part of the task force.
Trump said last week that he would set up a board to oversee AI safety after top tech bosses signed what he described as a "morally binding" pact to regulate the technology.

highlights.title: NJ’s former Lt Gov is using AI to say he’s innocent of sexual harassment
highlights.summary: New Jersey's lieutenant governor Dale Caldwell was forced to resign on September 25th after an investigation found he had sexually harassed a staffer and repeatedly violated ethics rules. The now-former Lt. governor has been making the media rounds trying to clear his name.
body: Dale Caldwell resigned over a sexual harassment investigation, but insists AI says he’s innocent.

Caldwell claims he’s being unfairly targeted, and multiple AI agents back that up. He told host Rob Nelson that he “AIed” the report on the investigation “from multiple AI platforms.” “I put it through AI,” he said, “and it said 59 times, it [sic] said, ‘What would your findings be?’ There was no instance in any of the AIs that said there would be a finding of sexual harassment.”

AI chatbots are notoriously sycophantic and often tell users what they want to hear. And it seems highly unlikely that Caldwell would want to hear an AI confirm findings that he engaged in sexual harassment.

body: I may be wrong but, a few years ago, I don't think Luke would have hung in a game like that to win it.
That was sheer belief: guts and determination knowing that you can do it - and he can do it against anyone from any position.

When you have won before, and Luke has done many, many times and in many, many ways, there is that belief of, 'I'm under pressure but let's just see as I know if I settle down my game can win', rather than 'oh no, I am going to get beat or get embarrassed 6-0'.
He played his game and he won. I am not saying it's that simple but sometimes you have to simplify it.

highlights.title: 10 Near-Perfect Nintendo Switch Games Nobody Played
highlights.summary: When a system has a library as diverse as the Nintendo Switch, some great games are bound to go unrecognized. There are thousands of physical titles available, and thousands more that never got more than a simple digital release. Not every game is for everyone, though.
body: A weekly cheat sheet to what you’ll eventually love to play. No buying, no commitment — just saving for later.

Capcom originally released Shinsekai: Into the Depths as an Apple Arcade title, but someone at the company later decided to port it to Switch, where the game delighted the players who gave it a chance with thrilling underwater exploration. Players must monitor their oxygen reserves while navigating the labyrinthine ruins of past civilizations, also relying on assistance from a robot who isn’t all that helpful. Satisfying Metroidvania design and beautiful environments will keep you coming back, even if the game’s mobile roots do show from time to time. Learn to ignore them and you should do just fine.

highlights.title: ‘Lanterns’ Ending Explained: How the Finale Sets Up John Stewart in 'Man of Tomorrow'
highlights.summary: The first episode of HBO’s Lanterns set up two big mysteries: What are extraterrestrials doing in Rushville, Nebraska, and who killed Hal Jordan (Kyle Chandler)? The season finale at long last reveals the truth about Hal’s death — along with more of Rushville’s secrets.
body: There has been plenty of speculation about who murdered Hal since his body was found in the stands of Rushville’s football stadium at the end of episode 1. However, episode 7 introduced the possibility that Hal might have shot himself in the head, following the sad “Jordan boys’ legacy” of his father and grandfather, who both died by suicide. But Hal actually seems very happy at the beginning of “Dirt and Stars,” where he’s hoping to take his relationship with Kerry Kane (Kelly Macdonald) to the next level by accompanying her to watch her son Noah (Shea Pritchard) play his last football game in Rushville.

Then someone sets Hal’s home on fire, and the former Green Lantern is trapped inside while trying to rescue his pet carnivorous plant Earl. Hal succumbs to smoke inhalation, but Noah rescues Hal from the fire and heals him with the same advanced technology Noah’s grandmother Zoe (Poorna Jagannathan) used on John Stewart (Aaron Pierre) in episode 5. Somehow, Earl also survives.

The season finale at long last reveals the truth about Hal’s death — along with more of Rushville’s secrets.

body: A slice of player spend from games including Clash of Clans, Brawl Stars, Clash Royale, Angry Birds 2, Golf Clash, Subway Surfers, Dream League Soccer, 8 Ball Pool and more will be donated to Special Effect for today only. A full list of participating games is available via the One Special Day site.

Special Effect provides assessments and customised technology loans to help physically disabled people play games, and takes what it learns back to hardware and software developers to help make their products more accessible. Thousands of disabled people ask for the charity’s help every year.

“We’ve been proud to partner with Special Effect across our games for nearly a decade, and that relationship has grown far beyond One Special Day,” said Supercell’s Deborah Mensah-Bonsu. “From cycling in Helsinki and joining One Special Walk in London, to learning from their incredible work as we think more deeply about inclusive design, we’re continually inspired by their tenacity, generosity and tremendous heart, and by how they show the games industry can genuinely change lives for the better.”

highlights.summary: SPOILER ALERT: This article contains spoilers for the “Lanterns” finale, now streaming on HBO Max. Have no fear, the “Lanterns” finale is here. The season finale — or possibly the series finale, since HBO hasn’t renewed the show yet — wrapped up the mystery posed by the show’s premiere of who…
body: In present day, back on the planet decimated by the Manhunters, John interrogates Sinestro (Ulrich Thomsen) and learns that Noah freed the villain from prison. Sinestro reveals that he harnessed the fear-inducing gas from the planet to create a new, yellow ring for Noah. As comics fans know, Sinestro is the creator of the Yellow Lanterns, an evil group opposed to the Green Lanterns who derive their power from fear. Sinestro offers John the chance to charge his depleted ring from the sinister, yellow lantern, but Hal’s hologram stops him, and they leave Sinestro marooned on the planet.

Noah ambushes John when he returns to Earth, the two drive back to Rushville together. Noah reveals that he didn’t burn down Hal’s house, but says he was the one who killed him. He claims he couldn’t let Hal reveal his identity as a Manhunter and the yellow lantern to Kerry. Noah says he’s trying to overcome his violent Manhunter programming, and asks that John kills him to protect everyone from what he might do. John doesn’t answer, but lets Noah go and play one last football game for Rushville.

highlights.title: Miu Miu turns ‘real clothes’ into high fashion with sportswear style
highlights.summary: Brand’s signature desire to subvert the ordinary brings blazers with track pants and crop tops under blazers to Paris fashion week. Speaking backstage at Miu Miu’s show on Sunday at Paris fashion week, Miuccia Prada said she had been thinking about “real clothes”.
body: The collection opened with a series of five neatly pleated checked skirts. The first was worn with an equally neat checked blazer but rather than a smart shoe, such as a pump or loafers, there were brightly coloured trainers. The second featured a crop top under the blazer, the trainers swapped for spiky high heels. The other looks ditched the blazer and clipped the tops so they sat just under the bust line.

Later came the type of track pants usually made for mooching around in; here they were paired with smart knitwear and tailored jackets. Gym knickers were given the same upgraded styling treatment, while sports bras were reimagined as sparkly tops, more party than pilates; some were worn solo, others over clingy jersey tops. Jeans, a collaboration with Wrangler to rework its vintage denim, hung low below hips. Instead of buttons, zips or even belts, there were fastenings that riffed on shoelaces.

Prada described the approach as “nonconformist dialogues exploring a form of friction and tension”. This method of clashing clothing genres and subverting the ordinary has turned Miu Miu into a near-billion-euro brand.

highlights.title: HBO Officially Changes a Fundamental Rule of Green Lantern Canon
highlights.summary: In HBO’s Lanterns, John Stewart (Aaron Pierre) spends his whole life preparing to become a Green Lantern. He seemingly abandons his destiny in episode 5, turning down the ring after becoming disillusioned with how the Guardians of the Universe treated the Manhunters and Hal Jordan (Kyle Chandler).
body: The Lanterns finale, “Dirt and Stars,” reveals that Sinestro (Ulrich Thomsen) forged a new Lantern on Antaan’s home planet. The planet’s air and water were contaminated by the Manhunter Zoe (Poorna Jagannathan), who unleashed a weapon that exposes people to their greatest fears and makes them suicidal. That fear manifests in yellow streaks in the Lantern.

“The Lantern Corp thinks that fear makes you weak,” Sinestro explains. “They couldn’t be more wrong. If harnessed correctly, fear can be the most powerful force in the universe. Fear is just evolutionary intelligence.”

The Halogram warns John not to use Sinestro’s Lantern to charge his ring, saying, “You don’t know what that Lantern might do.” But at the end of the episode, John uses the Lantern with a custom oath: “In brightest day, in darkest night, I embrace my fear, I’ll do what’s right. I choose this ring, I choose this fight, in service to this lantern’s light.” While he wants to use the power to protect Earth, John could be going down a very dark path.

highlights.title: ‘Lanterns’ Team Breaks Down Finale’s Emotional Gamble, Hal Jordan’s Ultimate Fate and John Stewart’s Future
highlights.summary: Some viewers might take issue with one major swing, but the team sees it as "remixing" rather than "rewriting" Green Lantern canon.
body: For a Lanterns season one finale that ends with John Stewart taking flight as his own brand of Green Lantern, it’s a rightfully grounded affair until then.

“There was never a version of the finale that was more action-oriented,” Lanterns showrunner Chris Mundy told moderator Mallory Rubin of The Ringer during the finale press conference, which featured the creative brain trust alongside stars Pierre and Chandler. “If we landed it emotionally with [Hal and John], we would’ve done our job. [Action for action’s sake] would’ve been distraction and incident instead of emotion.”
Structurally, co-creator Damon Lindelof considers episode five’s “Battle of Rushville” to be this series’ version of the CGI slugfest and sky-beam invasion we’ve seen time and time again.

“If we had to make a two-hour Lanterns movie, you would have to have a bombastic third-act action set piece — and then two or three minutes of coda,” Lindelof said. “We got to do that [coda] over the course of [the last] three episodes.”

highlights.title: Plot Twist! All the Books Guests Brought to the Valentino Show
highlights.summary: Alessandro Michele asked attendees to his spring 2027 show—titled Antibiblioteca: Catalogue of the Unread—to bring a book that would be donated to a local library.
body: Fashion week is built around looking, but Valentino wanted its guests to do a little reading, too.

While a show invitation usually tells you where to be, when to arrive, and sometimes offers a cryptic clue as to what awaits on the runway (for Dior, it was a walnut. At Schiaparelli, a Kandi friendship bracelet); at Valentino’s spring 2027 show, Alessandro Michele asked guests to bring along a book. “New or from your own library,” read the small green card tucked inside the invitation. After the show, the collected volumes would be donated to local libraries.

I’m bringing a memoir by Claude Billen (Delay), published in 1973, dedicated to her dear friend Gabrielle Chanel. Claude is Coco Chanel’s last surviving friend, and it’s fascinating to read about the greatest fashion icon through the eyes of a friend.

This is where I studied literature and breathed in freedom, convinced that the future belongs to women. But we must never let our guard down: Natalia Aspesi’s words in this 1978 book are more relevant today than ever.

highlights.title: Rural Data Centers Are in for a Big Federal Tax Break
highlights.summary: Under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, data center projects in rural areas could be eligible for major tax benefits starting next year. Some hyperscalers do not seem eager to take the free cash.
body: Welcome back to Power Play! Each week, senior writer Molly Taft tackles a topic around this midterm season’s biggest issue: data centers. If you’ve got a question or thought for the column, feel free to shoot Molly an email at [email protected] or reach them securely on Signal at mollytaft.76.
On January 1, a new tax windfall will kick in that could benefit scores of rural data center projects—all thanks to the One Big Beautiful Bill Act.

Starting next year, projects sited in tracts of rural land across the country will be newly eligible for a set of specific corporate tax benefits under a program expanded by the bill. The new rules “may significantly lower barriers for large-scale, capital-intensive projects in rural areas—most notably hyperscale data centers,” said a statement from Ways and Means Committee chair Jason Smith last year. “The economic case for building data centers in designated rural opportunity zones becomes far more compelling” with the new program, he continued.
But experts warn that the results for rural communities could be mixed.

The NFL is looking into the circumstances of an official swearing at Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride during the team’s loss to the New York Giants on Sunday, league spokesperson Brian McCarthy…
body: Line judge Jeff Seeman was caught on camera cursing at McBride, who appeared to laugh when he realized a camera had caught the incident. The interaction drew the ire of NFL Players Association executive director JC Tretter, a retired offensive lineman who played eight seasons in the league.

“This kind of behavior from an official towards a player is unacceptable,” Tretter said in a social media post which included a clip of the incident. “Players are consistently held accountable when the roles are reversed. We expect the NFL to hold officials to the same standard.”
The NFL Referees Association did not immediately respond to a message seeking comment.

The incident took place with just under five minutes left after officials did not call a penalty on New York’s Dru Phillips on a crucial third down, which the Cardinals did not convert. McBride questioned the call and Seeman appeared to respond to his appeal by saying “fuck you”. Arizona punted and the Giants went on to win the game 36-24. McBride did not address the incident in his postgame comments.

highlights.title: 10 Essential Sega Genesis Games Still Missing From Nintendo Switch Online
highlights.summary: Players who subscribe to Switch Online know that it comes with a wide variety of retro games from past Nintendo consoles such as the NES and SNES. If they opt to spend more for the Expansion Pass, they get access to games that appeared on additional hardware, including the Sega Genesis.
body: For a brief time there, Interplay was riding high on a brief series of personality-driven game releases. One of the wilder ones of the bunch was Boogerman: A Pick and Flick Adventure, which featured a comic superhero type who subdues his enemies with burps, farts, and boogers. The game relied heavily on gross-out humor, but featured competent platforming action to go with it, as well as vividly drawn characters who sold the joke. If you can look past the humor, you’ll find a solid experience that spans more than 20 levels, complete with puzzles and bosses. Nintendo made the game available on Virtual Console in 2008, but it hasn’t been seen since.

highlights.title: Does the word ‘Dumbass’ flash up when your husband calls your phone? | Polly Hudson
highlights.summary: From ‘Sharon London Sex’ to ‘Trashy Anne’, the names saved in our phones are tiny records of how relationships began. Why erase the evidence? At first glance, it’s such a simple, reasonable ask.
body: Personally, I’ve never got over noticing – on their reality show rather than while lunching – that Kim Kardashian has her mother saved as Kris Jenner instead of, say, Mom. It felt like an extremely revealing detail from the queen of the genre.

The Threads debate raised an interesting question, though: should your contact list be amended and updated, or preserved as a historical artefact? Perhaps the poster is underestimating the warm glow to the heart and soul he subconsciously receives whenever his wife’s name pops up and he’s transported back to the beginning of their unlikely love story. Living app-ily ever after is rare, after all.

Other replies echoed the notion that contacts provoke memories. “I’m coming up on the 10th anniversary of ‘Trashy Anne’ … who I got to know volunteering as bin collectors at a local festival,” said one. Another confided: “My best friend and I met through a mutual friend almost 15 years ago. I’m still ‘Ayannah (Gabby’s friend)’.” The comfort we get from a reminder of these origin stories may be more important than it seems.
points: From ‘Sharon London Sex’ to ‘Trashy Anne’, the names saved in our phones are tiny records of how relationships began.

body: Google’s midrange Fitbit Edge shows off is many sides and colors in leaked images.

Supposedly, this fitness-first wearable will have a seven-day battery life, as well as built-in GPS and an altimeter, making it far more capable than the minimalist Air. It will also have limited app support for things like Google Maps and YouTube Music. Beyond that, not a ton is known.

The Fitbit Charge line was last updated in 2023, so a new midrange tracker is long overdue. While we don’t have any word on price or release date yet, somewhere in the $150 to $200 range seems like a safe bet. The Air costs $99.99 and the Watch starts at $399.99, so the Edge would clearly fall somewhere in the middle. The Charge 6 currently goes for $159.95.

highlights.title: Mighty Mike Plays Dad Says He Owns 'Like 12 Companies,' Promises Refunds for AI Shirts
highlights.summary: Mighty Mike Plays dad Dave has promised refunds and issued a lengthy explanation after the internet demanded more information about the YouTube ads allegedly purchased by his son and the drama that followed.
body: The Mighty Mike Plays saga began when a father took to YouTube to announce that his son had allegedly used his company credit card to purchase more than $118,000 in video ads. It was a painful and highly relatable story that snowballed into a full-fledged internet spectacle when pricey AI-generated T-shirts and questionable details led many online to look for concrete answers.

The controversial father figure came clean in a new video titled " Allow me to Explain " that was uploaded to the Mighty Mike Plays channel last week (via Dexerto ). Dave started the hour-long explainer – which has since been deleted and re-uploaded on a new YouTube channel called Coffee Time with Dave – promising that everyone who purchased one of those T-shirts would receive a refund.

"Dave here. A.k.a. Devoted Dave. A.k.a. Dazzling Dave. A.k.a. Dependable Dave, and the list goes on," Dave said. "I want to give you guys an update: First off, I'm going to say that everyone that got a shirt got refunded whether they asked for it or not. So, whether you wanted a refund or not, you got it."

highlights.title: Björk Performs in the Mugler Collection She Inspired, the Same Day It Debuts in Paris
highlights.summary: For his third collection at Mugler, Miguel Castro Freitas looked to nature, animal instinct, and the radical freedom of Björk. In tandem, the Icelandic artist wore a look straight from the runway to the DJ booth in Poland.
body: In perhaps the most fashionable scheduling conflict ever, Björk couldn’t attend the latest Mugler show, one that she inspired, no less. Alas, she was in Bielsko-Biała, Poland, for the opening weekend of her touring exhibition Björk: Ancestress, Sorrowful Soil & Nerve Bloom (remix), performing a special DJ set that closed the Wędrujący Festiwal. So the Icelandic artist did the most Björk thing possible: she wore a look from the collection the same day it debuted in Paris. Who needs front-row pomp when you have a Polish market full of ravers?

For this latest rendezvous, styled by longtime collaborator Edda Guðmundsdóttir, Björk became Mugler’s satellite record-spinning model in a purple butterfly-print second-skin top and black leather corseted high-waisted skirt. Above it hovered a magnificent bit of house history: a fringed feather headpiece from Manfred Thierry Mugler’s spring 1997 haute couture collection, Les Insectes. The result collapsed nearly 30 years of Mugler into one silhouette: part woman, part extraterrestrial.

highlights.title: Prick’s theatrical industrial punk is perfect for spooky season
highlights.summary: While deep in the recording process for The Downward Spiral, Trent Reznor lent some of his production talents to old friend Kevin McMahon, from the new wave band Lucky Pierre (which Reznor was briefly a member of).
body: If Trent Reznor studied musical theater instead of computer engineering NIN might have sounded like Prick.

Opener “Communiqué” is a fuzzy blast of simple punk riffs with electronic sprinklings on top. McMahon’s vocals occasionally detour from the half-spoken verses that sound borrowed from a musical to full-throated Al Jourgensen-esque screams. The rough-around-the-edges production and focus on live instrumentation feel like a prototype for what Reznor would eventually revisit on With Teeth.

But it’s the second track, “Riverhead” where Reznor’s influences fully rear their head (even though he is not actually credited as the producer). The vocal melodies swerve like Outside - and Earthling -era Bowie around guitars that buzz with all the digital charr of the Broken EP. Then, around the three-minute mark, comes the breakdown. It slowly builds with layers of electronic drums, mechanical chords, and loping synthetic-sounding guitar melodies. The entire back chunk could easily have been a Downward Spiral or even The Fragile B-side.
These moments of richly layered production, though, are almost always immediately undermined, as with the sloppy garage-punk intro of “Tough”.

highlights.title: The Nvidia Shield TV Is 7 Years Old. It Just Got a $100 Price Hike
highlights.summary: The price of anything with memory is skyrocketing thanks to AI. Aging streaming devices are no exception.
body: The era of generative AI has upended technology supply chains, and there is one ironclad rule in 2026: If it has memory or storage, it’s getting more expensive. Even devices with years-old tech inside are still apparently subject to that unwritten rule. Nvidia has just announced that the Shield TV Pro is getting $100 more expensive, effective immediately.

The most recent version of the Shield streaming box debuted in 2019, running Android TV with AI upscaling and hardware decoding for almost any type of media. While it ran an aging Tegra X1+ processor, that was (and still is) fast for a TV media streamer. The device launched at $199.99, with a non-Pro variant at $149.99. The non-Pro Shield has since been discontinued, but the Shield TV Pro lives on at the new $299.99 price.

Nvidia has confirmed that you can blame AI for the higher Shield TV pricing. “Starting October 2, SHIELD Pro will be priced at $299. The cost of components, including memory, has increased substantially across the industry,” a spokesperson told Ars.

highlights.title: Australia’s Marnus Labuschagne set for South Africa Test after first ton in 11 months
highlights.summary: Batter makes 111 against Cricket South Africa Invitation XI. Three-match Test series starts in Durban on Friday. The indefatigable Marnus Labuschagne has responded to all the hand-wringing over whether he merits a place in Australia’s Test future by just doing what he likes doing best – scoring…
body: After a difficult year, the under-pressure 32-year-old chose the most timely moment to score his first century in any form of cricket for 11 months in Potchefstroom, just five days before Australia play their first Test in South Africa since the 2018 ball-tampering scandal.

Former skipper Ricky Ponting has led the chorus that Labuschagne’s Australia place has become “untenable” after three years and 43 Tests without a Test ton, capped by three failures in the recent Bangladesh series.

Yet the South Africa-born batter looks sure to fill the No 3 spot once more in the first Test that starts in Durban on Friday after his swift century against a modest Cricket South Africa Invitation XI attack on Sunday.

Labuschagne was largely untroubled as he raced to a 76-ball ton, going on to 111 from 89, decorated with 19 fours, before retiring to let his colleagues also get in some batting practice on the final day of the two-day warm-up match.

highlights.title: Blindfolded Tekken 8 Player Achieves One of the Game’s Top Ranks from Beginner
highlights.summary: Professional Tekken 8 player SuperBrine is going viral after reaching God of Destruction using Alisa while completely blindfolded with a sleep mask.
body: SuperBrine has been streaming his run on Twitch in the form of seven separate broadcasts, starting in June 2026. The final stream from this series, broadcast in early October, has become a hot topic within the fighting game community, as he was able to reach one of the game’s top ranks from Beginner while obscuring his vision with a sleep mask.

It’s an impressive feat no matter how you swing it, standing as a testament to SuperBrine’s skill as a player and Tekken 8’s laudable sound design — but, perhaps unsurprisingly, his blindfolded run from Beginner to God of Destruction has sparked no end of debate about the game's difficulty and Alisa’s ease of use as a character.

I got the chance to sit down with SuperBrine to discuss his self-imposed challenge and find out if it was legit or not. He confirmed that there was no way he was able to see through the sleep mask (which are typically made out of thick material with dense cushions on the eyes), and reiterated that he’d streamed his entire run live on Twitch for all to see, so there was no way for him to cheat.

highlights.title: Behind the Scenes: Duran Lantink Defines His Vision for Ready-to-Wear at Jean Paul Gaultier
highlights.summary: Vogue Business was a fly on the wall during creative director Lantink’s show fittings at the house HQ.
body: On the eve of his third ready-to-wear show for Jean Paul Gaultier, I met the house’s creative director, Duran Lantink, at the company’s headquarters on Rue Saint-Martin. Lantink works on fittings with London-based stylist Jodie Barnes.

I walk up the stairs and join him in a familiar space; this is where the couture shows take place. (Sunday’s ready-to-wear show is held at the Palais de Tokyo.) In the white-walled room with its high ceiling, there’s a model walking in low-rise jeans and a voluminous white top. “I like these jeans better than the ones before,” Barnes says. “Yes, and I like that the scorpion [the tattoo on the model’s belly] comes out,” Lantink adds.

Lantink was appointed creative director of the Puig-owned house in April 2025, assigned with leading both couture and ready-to-wear. Prior to his appointment, he helmed his eponymous label, founded in 2016, which joined the official fashion calendar in 2023. Barnes started working with the designer back then. “I love his raw talent. I think there’s a lot of freedom with him and the way he thinks, and I’m the same. Somehow, it comes together quite well,” she says.
points: Vogue Business was a fly on the wall during creative director Lantink’s show fittings at the house HQ.
